Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
TAMPERS AND RAMMERS FOR USE IN FOUNDRIES

l« Scope — Covers requirements for tampers, rammers and shoes for pneumatic rammers for use in 
foundries. 

2. Application — Tampers and rammers are used for preparing mould and cones. 

3. Dimensions — Dimensions and weights of the tools shall be as specified In Tables I to 5. 

4. Material 

4.1 Handle 

a) All tools except in Table 5 — Mild steel or cast iron with threaded ends. 

b) For tools in Table 5 — Any seasoned hard wood. 

4.2 Tamper and Rammer Heads — Mild steel. 

4.3 Combined Tamper and Rammer — Mild steel. 

4.4 Shoe for Rubber Tipped Pneumatic Rammer — Mild steel. 

4.5 V-S/ioe and Disc Shoe — Grey cast iron Grade 15, 15:210-1962 'Specification for grey iron castings 
{revised)'. 

4.6 Rubber Tip of Pneumatic Rammer — As required by the purchaser. 

5. Tolerances — Coarse class in 15:2102-1969 'Allowable deviations for dimensions without specified 
tolerances ( first revision ) \ 

6. Coating — Steel and Iron components shall be coated with protective paint. Wooden components 
shall be coated with suitable varnish. 

7. Marking-— Mark with the following: 

a) Designation, and 

b) Name or trade-mark of the manufacturer. 

7.1 ISI Certification MQri<.ing — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution, New Delhi I. 

8. Pacicing— The tools shall oe packed in wooden boxes weighing not more than 50 kg overalf. 

9. Supply — As specified in IS: 1387-1967 'General requirements for the supply of metallurgical materials 
( first revision ) '. 

10. Fitting 

iO.I The handles of tools in Tables I, 2 and 3 shall be welded to the he^ds. Alternatively handles in 
Tables I, 2 and 3 may be fixed by screwing in the rammer heads. 

10.2 For tools in Table 5, the handle shall be secured to the head by countersunk screws conforming to 
M 4 of IS: 1365-1968 'Slotted countersunk head and slotted raised countersunk head screws (dia range 1*6 
to 20 mm) {second reWs/on)' in the black condition. 

10.3 Any other screws used for other tools shall have the same nominal size as mentioned in the drawing. 
They shall conform to IS: 1365-1968 in the black condition.-
